462493170453287_554497441252859.text: Fred Palmer August 30, 1979 is the day the company I worked for caused an accident that threw six men out of a train that had derailed because of their negligence. Since then I have been physically disabled from any type labour work and am at risk of blood clots in my leg if I stand or walk too long. I don't mind that so much as the physical and emotional abuse they make me suffer from. There is a condition called "Chronic Pain" that is a result of the extensive nerve damage they gave me that has literally almost killed me because the company, WSIB/WCB, other government agencies such as Eastern Health and Welfare will not treat me properly and timely for my condition. I was also brain injured because of my companies negligence in the same accident and cannot accept any stress from them, yet that is all they give me. Because as an injured worker my rights have been taken by my governments I cannot get justice, get medical care, get financial compensation for my lost wages, and have been bullied, threatened, forced into poverty no matter what I try to do to get well and back to work at some type of job. For 34 years now I have been held hostage to tyranny in its most insidious and evil form, the taking of my rights. I will not appeal, cannot appeal, and according to WSIB I am dead and have to prove I am alive. I will not prove anything to them. They already know my condition and have used that never been married, have no family, no property, am extremely upset emotionally, disillusioned, disappointed, and have had my whole life stolen from me by what can only be called discrimination and neglect. Today I live for only one reason. To destroy the WSIB and any agency or government that would abuse a man or woman to death for money. I will never give up until I am dead and even then I will not stop. Maybe my life is a piece of crap but I don't want you or your families to suffer the horrors of compensation abuse like I am. I cannot as a human being, knowing how WSIB murders its patients, take part in or ignore such a serious issue. 34 years of abuse and pain and suffering has taught me a lot. I am a good man, a valuable, and kind and generous man. A lovely man who has empathy and concern for his fellow human beings. I just wish government had one tenth of this and we would suffer no more. To that end I have committed my life, no matter my poverty, no matter my pain and suffering. For you. For mankind's future. For all of us. Today I celebrate me.
